content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, T4C).**

**What I found.** The termination architecture sits in the mis-numbered tail of the Indemnity section:

- **§ 13 (p0078)** — 1-year term, auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, with mutual non-renewal on 30 days' notice before year-end. Vendor's only convenience-style exit is end-of-term non-renewal, which is acceptable under our playbook, so I left it alone.
- **§ 14 (p0079)** — references a "Client election to terminate," but it is drafted as a *service-continuation mechanic*, not a right: it never says Client may terminate without cause, the effective date floats between ~30 and ~60 days depending on where in the month notice lands, it is made "Subject to Section 4" (a section that does not exist in the document, apparently the minimum-monthly-fee provision), and it is silent on refunds and on early-termination/minimum-fee exposure.
- **Cross-reference defects** — § 13 routes termination to "Section 12" (Indemnity), and § 2.c (p0028) says the license runs until termination "in accordance with section 12." Our exit right points at the wrong clause.

**Why this is a deviation rather than compliant.** Fees are billed monthly in arrears (§ 5.a, p0045), so refund exposure is modest — but the "Subject to Section 4" hook plus the undefined minimum monthly fees creates a real argument that we owe minimum fees after notice, which is exactly the penalty the playbook targets. Combined with the absence of an express, unambiguous convenience right, this falls short of the preferred position.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Rewrote § 14 as an express 30-day Client convenience right, in whole or in part, with payment only through the effective date, a refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination fee or minimum-fee obligation, and an express bar on TrueLink terminating for convenience mid-term. Also corrected § 13's cross-reference from Section 12 to Section 14. Confidence 0.78.

Two judgment calls worth your review: I deleted the "Subject to Section 4" hook rather than preserving it, since the referenced section is absent and its only plausible reading works against us — if Section 4 exists in an unshared exhibit, that deletion should be revisited. I also left § 2.c's parallel bad cross-reference unfixed to keep the edit minimal; it may be worth sweeping in the same round.
